title: XTP dev34 encrypted named-service read ingress
summary: Bind source-side Memory Fabric read admission to native XTP34 encrypted-message metadata, an active LDAP-derived service key principal and an independent current block/range ACL. This is an executable adapter with a synthetic transport fixture, not a qualified live remote read server.
invariants: Only native XtpNamedAcceptedSocket results from a locally configured listener are admissible; request payloads cannot assert service, principal, key, route or operational class.
Require protection=encrypt and a current, non-expired, non-revoked key in the locally authoritative XtpServiceKeys registry; no missing-key or LDAP outage downgrade to clear.
Remote memory service keys must originate in the estate Identity Directory over LDAP; local key-file fallback may preserve transport but cannot authorize a memory read by itself.
The key principal is a service-key identity and must be uniquely provisioned and independently authorized by the Memory Fabric block/range ACL; XTP AEAD alone is not Memory Fabric authorization.

Frame MFXR1 rejects malformed/overlong/partial reads, and the Memory Fabric ingress gate rechecks ACL, current block generation, owning provider epoch and current key for each page before publication.
XTP dev34 one-way protected message replay across distinct listeners sharing a key is a known risk; never infer distributed exactly-once from the process-local replay cache or network ACK.
XTP dev34 multicast has no service group-key protection: never send confidential memory bytes to a multicast group without a separately qualified mechanism.
Local MI-MU Layer-2 and DMA/shared-memory paths remain separate; remote L2/raw36/UDP are XTP carrier concerns, not application service identities.
Native dev34 read callback/actual page response, live LDAP/Secret Broker, Gopher activation and ED209 field testing remain acceptance gates, not inherited passes.
procedure: Install the dev34 XTP native library and the estate XtpServiceKeys LDAP/Secret Broker source; refresh keys before binding the named memory read service.
Construct MemoryXtp34KeyAuthenticator with the local live key registry and trusted epoch-second clock.
Create MemoryXtpReadIngress with Memory Fabric dev10 registry, Service Descriptor Registry, authenticator and actual block/range ACL.
From a trusted native named-service listener, pass the accepted XTP object and trusted epoch-millisecond clock to MemoryXtp34ReadBridge~admitReceived.
Validate the returned read permit immediately before every page access and again before publishing page bytes. Audit all denials without exposing key material.

provenance.claim: Implements strict protected ingress, live local service key verification, bounded wire decode and read permit handoff; local test uses a fixture.
XTP dev34 upstream native encrypted-message and replay security path (upstream file hash from VALIDATION_DEV34.txt; not separately qualified here).
